title: Rav Huna son of Rav Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: His father is mentioned in [Yoma 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.6b.4): Rav Tachlifa, father of Rav Huna bar Tachlifa, transmits a teaching in Rava’s name. Hyman says that he too always spoke in Rava’s name, as in Yevamot 8a (compare [Yevamot 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.8b.6)), [Bava Metzia 35a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.35a.5) and [Niddah 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.26a.9); in [Kiddushin 71a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.71a.15) Hyman calls “in Rav’s name” erroneous and proposes “in Rava’s name.”
In [Zevachim 77a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.77a.5), Rav Rechumi transmits a teaching in Rav Huna bar Tachlifa’s name before Ravina.[^2]

notes.text: Hyman’s always-in-Rava’s-name assertion retains its strength, and the proposed Rav-to-Rava correction remains attributed. Rav, Rava and the father/son distinction are not harmonized.

The Yoma report names Tachlifa, Huna’s father, in Rava’s name. In Bava Metzia and Niddah Huna himself transmits in Rava’s name. Kiddushin has Rav as authority. In Zevachim Huna is the authority quoted by Rechumi before Ravina. The Yevamot teaching is at 8b, as Heilprin records. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1004&lang=en).
